summary.title: How Facebook Build Products
summary.one_liner: Learn how Facebook's product managers split strategy from execution, use "meta-execution" to delegate work, and why empowered product teams are judged on outcomes rather than tasks.
takeaways: A PM at Facebook is accountable for two outcomes: strategy (choosing what game to play) and execution (how to play it).
Execution splits into prioritization (roadmapping, impact estimates, feature choice) and process management; junior PMs often spend most of their time on the latter.
Meta-execution means delegating execution to capable leaders on the team so the PM can focus on work only they can do and on longer-term strategy.
In empowered product teams, the team decides what to build and is judged on outcomes, so engineers and others often drive parts of execution, and the PM remains accountable for results.
summary.summary: This is a personal blog essay by a Facebook product manager responding to a viral debate about PMs' day-to-day work. It defines the PM role as strategy plus execution, breaks execution into prioritization and process management, and argues that PMs should be judged on team outcomes rather than inputs such as Gantt charts or meeting notes. It then covers "meta-execution" (delegating to leaders), how engineers and PMs share execution work on empowered teams, and draws on Marty Cagan's empowered vs non-empowered team distinction. The piece is opinion and experience-based, with no code or tooling.
